introduction: Secrets and variables are named values kept for a user, an organization or a workspace. They share their key, size, count and ordering rules; they differ in that a secret's value never comes back out, and in the access a workspace's entries need.

glossary.entry scope: One owner of secret or variable entries: one user, one organization or one workspace. Each holds at most 100 entries and keys are unique within it, ignoring case. Distinct from a permission scope, which is a named permission on a credential.
glossary.origin: The tier a resolved variable's value came from: user, org or workspace.
glossary.resolved view: The merge of a workspace's variables with those of its organization and of its owner, a workspace value overriding an organization value, which overrides a user value.
glossary.secret: A named value kept for a user, an organization or a workspace whose value is never returned by any route, log record or audit event.
glossary.variable: A named value with the same rules as a secret, whose value is returned.

requirements.title: Rules shared by both kinds at every scope
requirements.rationale: Six rules repeated across twenty-five routes; implemented once they hold everywhere, implemented per route they drift.

criteria.action: accept a key only when it holds letters, digits and underscores, does not start with a digit, and is at most 255 characters
criteria.contract: a conforming key is accepted; a key with a hyphen, a space, a dot, a leading digit, an empty key or one of 256 characters is refused 400 and writes nothing

criteria.action: match keys case-insensitively, both when looking an entry up and when deciding whether one already exists in the scope
criteria.contract: an entry created as MY_KEY is found by my_key and MyKey; a create of my_key in a scope already holding MY_KEY is refused as a duplicate

criteria.condition: a value is larger than 262144 bytes
criteria.action: refuse the request and write nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; a value of exactly 262144 bytes is accepted and one of 262145 is refused

criteria.condition: a create would take a scope past 100 entries
criteria.action: refuse the whole request and write none of its entries
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; the scope still holds the entries it held before, and a create that brings it to exactly 100 succeeds

criteria.action: return every list sorted by key, ignoring case
criteria.contract: for keys differing only in case and in letter, the order is the case-insensitive ascending order of the keys

requirements.title: Secrets at the three scopes
requirements.rationale: The scopes differ in who may reach them, and a workspace's secrets are private in a way its variables are not.

criteria.condition: a create is called at any of the three secret scopes with one or more entries
criteria.action: store each entry and answer with the created entries, carrying no value
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with an array of {key, created_at, updated_at}; no element carries a value key

criteria.condition: a list, replace or delete is called at any of the three secret scopes
criteria.action: list the scope's keys, replace one entry's value, or remove one entry
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {key, created_at, updated_at} for a list, HTTP 200 with the entry for a replace, HTTP 204 for a delete; no response carries a value

criteria.action: admit the user secret routes to a user credential only, the organization secret routes to members of that organization and admin tokens, and the workspace secret routes at private access
criteria.contract: an admin token on a user secret route is 403; a non-member on an organization secret route is 404; a member of the workspace's organization on a workspace secret route is 404, as a stranger is

criteria.condition: a create names a key the scope already holds ignoring case
criteria.action: refuse the whole request and write none of its entries
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 in the error envelope; the existing entry's value and updated_at are unchanged, and no other entry of the same request is written

criteria.condition: a replace carries no value, or a replace or delete names a key the scope does not hold, or the named organization or workspace cannot be reached
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for a missing value, HTTP 404 for an unknown key and for an unreachable organization or workspace; the scope's entries are unchanged

requirements.title: Variables at the three scopes
requirements.rationale: Variables share every rule with secrets except the two that matter: their values come back, and a workspace's are readable by a member.

criteria.condition: a create, list or replace is called at any of the three variable scopes
criteria.action: answer with the entries including their values
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 on create and 200 on list and replace, each element carrying {key, value, created_at, updated_at}; HTTP 204 on delete

criteria.action: apply the same key, value-size, entry-count and ordering rules to variables as to secrets
criteria.contract: the key, size, count and duplicate refusals of the secret routes answer identically on the variable routes

criteria.action: require read access to read a workspace's variables and write access to change them
criteria.contract: a member of the workspace's organization lists and reads them as the owner does

criteria.condition: a member of the workspace's organization creates, replaces or deletes a workspace variable
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden and the message "org members have read-only access to this workspace"; the workspace's variables are unchanged

criteria.action: treat a variable whose key matches the name of a workspace setting as an ordinary variable that governs no behaviour
criteria.contract: setting a variable named like a setting changes no value in the workspace's settings object and alters no behaviour the settings control

requirements.title: The resolved view
requirements.rationale: It is computed from the workspace's owner rather than the caller, so a caller-centred implementation passes every owner test and is still wrong.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved is requested by a caller with read access
criteria.action: merge the three tiers, a workspace value overriding an organization value and an organization value overriding a user value, and report where each surviving value came from
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {key, value, origin, created_at, updated_at}, origin being user, org or workspace; a key set at all three tiers appears once with the workspace's value and origin workspace

criteria.action: take the user tier from the workspace's owner, never from the caller
criteria.contract: a variable set only in the caller's own user scope does not appear; one set only in the owner's user scope appears with origin user; the answer is identical whoever with read access asks

criteria.condition: the workspace's owner is not a member of the workspace's organization
criteria.action: leave the organization tier out of the merge
criteria.contract: a variable set only at that organization's scope does not appear in the resolved view

criteria.action: return the resolved view sorted by key, ignoring case
criteria.contract: the array is in case-insensitive ascending key order whatever the tier each value came from

requirements.title: Keeping a secret secret
requirements.rationale: A secret that can be read back from a route, a log or the database is not a secret, and that is the whole difference between the two kinds.

criteria.action: return no secret's value from any route, including the create and replace routes that just received it
criteria.contract: for any secret route and any scope, no response body contains the value that was stored

criteria.action: encrypt a secret's value before it reaches any store
criteria.contract: after a secret with a distinctive value is written, a raw dump of the underlying store contains no occurrence of that value

criteria.action: keep secret values out of every log record
criteria.contract: after a create, a replace, a refused create and a request that raises an unhandled failure, no log record contains the value

execution_paths.title: An owner stores a workspace secret and can never read it back

steps.action: creates a secret in a workspace's scope with a distinctive value
validates the key, checks the scope's entry count, encrypts the value and writes it through the secret store
answers 201 with the key and its timestamps and no value
lists the workspace's secrets and sees the key with no value
inspects the raw store and finds no occurrence of the value

execution_paths.title: Variables resolve from the workspace outwards

steps.action: sets one key at the owner's user scope, the same key at the organization's scope and at the workspace's scope, and a second key at the user scope alone
merges the owner's user tier, the organization tier and the workspace tier and reports each value's origin
finds the first key once with the workspace's value and origin workspace, and the second with origin user

execution_paths.title: A member reads a workspace's variables and is refused its secrets and its writes

steps.action: lists the workspace's variables and is served with their values
creates a workspace variable and is refused 403 forbidden
applies read access to the variable list and write access to the variable create
lists the workspace's secrets and is refused 404, because that route needs private access
